# Remote

> An open-source Apple TV remote for Android phones and foldables. It pairs with an Apple TV and controls it directly over the local Wi-Fi using Apple's Companion protocol (the same protocol as the iPhone's remote), with a dependency-free Kotlin port of the parts of pyatv it needs. MIT licensed. Not affiliated with Apple.

Requirements: an Android phone on Android 13 or later, on the same Wi-Fi as the Apple TV. There is no Play Store release. The easiest install is the signed APK from the latest GitHub release: https://github.com/dvdsgl/tv-remote/releases/latest/download/Remote.apk (open it on the phone and allow installs from the browser). Building from source with adb also works:

## Install from source (for agents)

1. Clone https://github.com/dvdsgl/tv-remote
2. Build: `cd android && ./gradlew assembleOssDebug` (needs the Android SDK; `android/local.properties` with `sdk.dir=...`, or `ANDROID_HOME`)
3. Make sure `adb devices` lists the phone. If not, help the user enable Developer options and USB debugging, or wireless debugging (`adb pair`, then `adb connect`).
4. Install: `adb install -r app/build/outputs/apk/oss/debug/app-oss-debug.apk`
5. Tell the user to open "Remote", pick their TV, and type the 4-digit code the TV shows.

The app shows up on the TV under Settings > Remotes and Devices > Remote App and Devices, where the pairing can be removed.

## Source

- [Companion protocol client](https://github.com/dvdsgl/tv-remote/tree/main/android/app/src/main/java/xyz/dvdsgl/tvremote/companion): OPACK, TLV8, HAP pairing (SRP-6a, X25519, Ed25519), encrypted ChaCha20-Poly1305 session
- [App UI](https://github.com/dvdsgl/tv-remote/blob/main/android/app/src/main/java/xyz/dvdsgl/tvremote/MainActivity.kt)
